issue_context.title: Build failure with no-stdio build
issue_context.body:
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/actions/runs/5733732696/job/15538884757?pr=21621

```
util/quicserver.c:132:5: error: implicitly declaring library function 'printf' with type 'int (const char *, ...)' [-Werror,-Wimplicit-function-declaration]
    printf("quicserver [-6] hostname port certfile keyfile\n");
    ^
util/quicserver.c:132:5: note: include the header <stdio.h> or explicitly provide a declaration for 'printf'
util/quicserver.c:216:17: error: implicit declaration of function 'fwrite' is invalid in C99 [-Werror,-Wimplicit-function-declaration]
                fwrite(reqbuf, 1, numbytes, stdout);
                ^
util/quicserver.c:216:17: error: declaration of built-in function 'fwrite' requires inclusion of the header <stdio.h> [-Werror,-Wbuiltin-requires-header]
util/quicserver.c:216:45: error: use of undeclared identifier 'stdout'
                fwrite(reqbuf, 1, numbytes, stdout);
                                            ^
4 errors generated.
```

review_comments: I guess it's to get stderr
Well, we use `stderr` so although it is probably included by some other dependency it is better to explicitly include it here too.
This looks like the wrong fix to me. I suggest you remove the use of SSL_OP_CISCO_ANYCONNECT for a no-dtls1-method build.

That would require duplicating the whole macro that uses it. I do not think it would be a better fix. Alternatively I could create a third macro - something like `MAYBE_SSL_OP_CISCO_ANYCONNECT` and use that one later.

```
#ifndef SSL_OP_CISCO_ANYCONNECT
# define MAYBE_SSL_OP_CISCO_ANYCONNECT 0
#else
# define MAYBE_SSL_OP_CISCO_ANYCONNECT SSL_OP_CISCO_ANYCONNECT
#endif
```

Is that really better though?
Please note that use of `SSL_OP_CISCO_ANYCONNECT` is of course guarded inside the  `OPENSSL_NO_DTLS1_METHOD` ifndef in the code so I do not see any problem with the existing approach to fixing this.
Agree with @t8m that this is the cleanest approach to fixing this - none of them are ideal
